name: gel-wash
title: Gel Wash
description: Full-page preloader built like a stage lantern — three coloured gels breathing over a blackout, pulled off one at a time when the page is ready.
useWhen: A first-paint or route-transition curtain that has to hold the page back for a beat and then leave with some colour in it. Reach for one of the inline loaders (blade-iris, lath-rack, phase-swing) when only a region is pending — this one owns the whole viewport and locks scroll, which is wrong for anything smaller than a page.
instruction: A full-viewport preloader staged like a theatre lantern: one opaque blackout layer in the background token, and in front of it three fixed colour gels — blue, cyan, magenta — each a soft radial wash placed off-centre so they overlap into secondaries rather than reading as three separate blobs. While the page is not ready the gels breathe on opacity and a slight scale, each on its own period (2.6s, 3.3s, 4.0s) and its own delay, so the field never pulses in unison and never settles into a loop the eye can count. Blend mode carries the two themes: multiply in light so the gels behave like real coloured film over paper, screen in dark so they behave like light. The exit is the whole point of the component — the blackout is pulled first and fastest (560ms), so the last thing a visitor sees is coloured light sweeping up off real content rather than a panel disappearing over nothing, and the three gels follow on staggered durations (720/880/1040ms) and 90ms delays so the lantern empties gel by gel. Two things gate the exit rather than one: the caller's own `ready` flag AND a minimum on-screen time (`minMs`, default 900), because a load that finishes in 40ms would otherwise flash a curtain, which reads as a bug rather than as polish. While it is up, body scroll is locked with the vanishing scrollbar's width compensated as padding so the page doesn't jump sideways when the lock releases, and the overlay carries role=status with aria-busy, dropping aria-busy the moment the exit begins and going pointer-events:none for the whole exit so a click during the sweep lands on the page underneath. The component unmounts itself once the last gel is clear and fires onDone. Under prefers-reduced-motion the breathing stops and the exit is instant — the wash still holds the page for its minimum, it just does not perform.
